__comment: Shelter settles the temperature at the land's own annual mean, and depth warms it back up.
Priority 90, below the altitude definition's 100, so this runs last of everything. That is what
lets a deep cave under a mountain blend the mountain's cold away: rock does not care how high it
The settled temperature is mean_temperature + degrees_per_biome_temperature x the biome's own
vanilla temperature, so it is derived rather than judged by name - the same source the pack's
climate bands were derived from. Snowy plains (0.0) settle at 8 C, plains (0.8) at 12.8, jungle
(0.95) at 13.7, desert (2.0) at 20. Every one of those is inside the comfort band, which is the
point: a cave is a refuge from both ends.
Depth adds 0.08 C per block below sea level, capped at 12 C, so the bottom of the world sits
around 20-32 C depending on what is above it. Warm, and still short of the 35 C heat threshold.
full_shelter_depth is the field that stops this becoming central heating. Sky light alone would
make any hut a climate-controlled room; requiring 16 blocks of world overhead as well means a
house takes the edge off a blizzard without ending it. See CaveShelter.java.
